paragraphs: I was allowed to study abroad for three months at the Medical University of Gdańsk together with 宗宮. For me, who had originally not been very good at English, this study abroad was a kind of challenge. Because the seniors in my club went abroad somewhere every year, I had wanted to study abroad myself since early in university. The reason I chose Poland was that the seniors who went to the Medical University of Gdańsk last year seemed to be having a great time and that clerkships in English were well developed. Thanks also to the relationships accumulated by seniors every year, I was able to lead a good study abroad life to the end. I would like to introduce that life.

First, as for the clerkship content, I was allowed to rotate through a different department every one to two weeks. Specifically I was allowed to rotate through many departments: neonatology, obstetrics and gynecology, hypertension and diabetes, hematology, pediatrics, ophthalmology and pediatric surgery. As for the form of the clerkship, there was first a lecture in each department, followed by bedside clerkship. The lectures were not very different in content from Japan, but because epidemiology is very different, there were several times when the diseases explained with emphasis differed from Japan. Also, what I felt in neonatology, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics and pediatric surgery was that Japanese medicine has advanced more than I had imagined. Even for diseases with single-digit mortality in Japan, nearly half died in Poland. It was astonishing to learn that something I had thought rarely kills can easily kill if circumstances change. I think that being able to realize the blessing that becomes numb when one is in Japan will be nourishment in the future.

Many of the patients themselves could not speak English, so examinations were done with the doctors interpreting, but I was allowed to see many patients even though the doctors were busy. In Poland history taking is considered important, and I was often asked by the doctors what I should elicit. Because the country is not that wealthy, I got the impression that they aim to diagnose and treat as cheaply as possible. In the choice of each drug too, the drug price was discussed alongside duration of effect and side effects. I think it was of great value to be able to feel many differences from the Japanese medical situation in this way. At the end of each department there was an examination, and I studied for it every day, so there was a moderate stimulus. Being able to lead the clerkship life while keeping my motivation in this way was also a point that made me glad about this university.

In my life during the study abroad I tried to live as if I were a local as much as possible. I cooked for myself as much as possible and joined in various things without refusing when invited. Thanks to the daily necessities that the seniors left behind, I was able to live comfortably for three months. I was looked after by Professor Wozniak, who runs this study abroad program, and assistant professor Adam, who took me out to meals and helped me in situations where Polish was needed. I was allowed to give a presentation on the effects of green tea hosted by Professor Wozniak, and I was treated to traditional dishes at the professor's home.

In addition, many local students invited me to play and drink, and I was allowed to live fulfilling days. I also contacted a local badminton group and was allowed to join their practice every week. The language barrier was thick, but with people who could speak English I had the opportunity to eat and drink together, and I think it was good that I took part actively. On weekends and consecutive holidays I traveled to other countries, and even there I was able to interact with local people and other travelers, which was a lot of fun.

It was a study abroad in which I was astonished that one's world expands this much with just a little English, and in which I keenly felt that nearly all the important information can be obtained only in English. In the three months I was able to have so many experiences that I cannot write them all here, and I think it was truly good that I went. Finally, thank you very much to the International Collaboration Office and everyone who supported this study abroad.
